card.name: Equivalence and biosimilarity wording
card.fires_on: Inside or just before words about equivalence between two products, such as equivalent, bioequivalent, biosimilarity and non-inferiority. It appears in label text comparing formulations or a biosimilar with its reference product.

modes.label: Equivalent after clinically/therapeutic
modes.description: The word equivalent or its stem, used when comparing two formulations.
modes.example: have been demonstrated to be clinically<< equivalent>> to 2 mg sirolimus tablets

modes.label: Partway through biosimilar or bioequivalent
modes.description: The middle piece of bio- words that state two products match.
modes.example: Bios<<im>>ilarity of KIRSTY has been demonstrated

modes.label: Non-inferiority
modes.description: The middle of non-inferiority in trial results.

card.writes: It seems to help finish comparison words such as comparator and alternative, which fit comparing one product with another.
card.plain: It spots words saying one drug product is equivalent or comparable to another.
